questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and expect oncoming traffic to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in the direction of the arrow. But you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, who have the green light.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street, whether it is a marked or unmarked crosswalk. Always yield to pedestrians crossing any street for safety.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slow enough to stop within the area your headlights shine on.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep your dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slow enough to stop within the area your headlights shine on.
questions.explanation: You cannot see as far ahead at night as during the day. Slow down so you can stop your vehicle within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: You may cross a single solid white line on the highway:

options.text: When traffic conditions require you to do so.
Only to turn into a driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic conditions require you to do so.
questions.explanation: You may cross a single solid line to pass other vehicles or change lanes, but only when road conditions or traffic make it necessary.

questions.question: Which of the following helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows painted in lanes show drivers which lanes to use for specific actions, like driving straight or turning.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane on a two-lane road going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. You should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic can flow.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move into the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for faster driving, passing, and turning left. Use the right lane for slower driving, entering the road, and turning right.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking on a downward slope, turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic and hit the curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Hiking trails ahead to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against your seat back and place your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas of the road freeze first and thaw last on cold, wet days. These spots are more likely to be icy.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: In general, you should pass vehicles going the same direction by passing on their:

options.text: Only if the other driver signals that it is safe.
Whenever you have the opportunity to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to pass. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When exiting an interstate, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: When leaving an interstate, keep your speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the speed posted for the exit ramp.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car if it blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. This prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: A solid white line on the road's right edge angles toward the center. This means:

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will be required to turn left just ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line shows the edge of the road. When this line angles toward the center, it means the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, roadwork trucks, or horse-drawn carriages. It looks orange during the day and red at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: You can pass on the right when the way ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline allows you to pass another vehicle on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: On average, how long does it take your body to process one 12-ounce beer?
questions.correctAnswerText: One hour.
questions.explanation: On average, your body processes one 12-ounce beer, 5 ounces of wine, or 1.5 ounces of hard liquor in about one hour. Women's bodies may process alcohol more slowly, resulting in higher alcohol levels for longer.

questions.question: If you turn left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to where you came from.
